notes.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they targeted a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, in retaliation for an air attack on a telecom tower in Sirik. No immediate US or Bahraini comment.
notes.key: claim:iran revolutionary guard corps statement via tasnim
notes.claim_by: party:Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps statement via Tasnim

notes.fact: Euronews reports Iran's Guards announced via state media that they destroyed the radar; Qatar- and Pakistan-mediated diplomacy continues, and Tehran makes formal talks conditional on its demands.
notes.key: claim:iran revolutionary guard corps via state media
notes.claim_by: party:Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps via state media

notes.fact: Seoul broadcaster SBS, citing Reuters and AFP, says neither Washington nor Manama confirmed the radar claim. Iran wants the port blockade lifted and an oil-sanctions waiver before reopening Hormuz.
Israel's i24 reports Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran and asked Vance to focus on other tasks instead of Tehran negotiations.
notes.event: Trump sidelines Vance on Iran talks

notes.fact: Gulf News relays a Wall Street Journal report that Vance was weighing face-to-face talks with Iran's Mohsen Rezaei; no date was set. This conflicts with Trump's Nov 12 post.
notes.event: Trump sidelines Vance on Iran talks

notes.fact: South Front, which carried Trump's remarks, says he would have no hesitation about renewed force and that the US naval blockade of Iranian ports stays.
notes.event: Trump sidelines Vance on Iran talks

notes.fact: The New Arab says Trump held off further strikes on Iran at Gulf allies' request, while diplomats scramble to avert a return to war.
notes.event: Trump sidelines Vance on Iran talks

notes.fact: UKMTO confirmed a tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz and reclassified it as an attack; all crew safe.
notes.key: claim:ukmto uk royal navy run body

notes.fact: UKMTO reported a tanker hit about 19 nautical miles northeast of Limah, Oman, on Nov 10. ADNOC Logistics said one of its vessels was damaged in an attack in UAE waters.
Iran's state-linked Mehr agency reports Iran's army says two tankers that violated its route rules were set on fire in the strait on Nov 10.
A Hormuz tracker counts at least 23 vessels struck since Oct 1 and says Brent settled at $98.32, down 13.3% on the week. It cites Windward and Kpler counts of 40-42 daily transits.
Putin met US envoys Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow after the Abu Dhabi talks; Witkoff said trilateral talks restarted and a new meeting is set.
notes.event: Putin meets US envoys after Abu Dhabi

notes.fact: Russian state outlet RT says delegation head Medinsky announced agreement in principle on a large prisoner exchange, which Kushner and Ukraine's Umerov confirmed. Russia's state media says no European envoys sat in.
The National says Putin told the envoys he is not opposed to peace but rejected European peacekeepers, calling them legitimate targets. EU leaders in Dublin welcomed renewed momentum.
notes.key: claim:putin as relayed by reports from moscow
notes.claim_by: party:Putin (as relayed by reports from Moscow)

notes.fact: Kyiv Independent reports Ukrainian drones hit the Lukoil Volgograd refinery and a Rostov-on-Don facility overnight; the regional governor confirmed a massive attack and fires. Kyiv had not commented.
Volgograd governor Bocharov says four plant workers died and two were hospitalised, blaming drone debris. Meduza reports fuel queues in the city and that it could not confirm the plant.
Russia's defence ministry says it destroyed 1,198 Ukrainian drones overnight. Moscow's mayor says 467 flew toward the Moscow region and all four Moscow airports were restricted.
Euromaidan Press, citing Reuters, says Ukrainian strikes since Oct 30 had disrupted about 30% of Russian refining capacity by Nov 10.
Kenyan outlet Streamline Feed, relaying Reuters, says a US-announced energy ceasefire failed to hold in late October and cumulative strikes knocked out roughly 30% of Russian refining.

AFP, via a Philippine outlet, reports Yemeni security sources say Houthi missiles and a drone targeted coalition and Yemeni camps in Aden on Nov 11. The coalition says it downed three cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh.
notes.event: Houthi strikes on Aden and Riyadh

notes.fact: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted drones toward Mecca; a Houthi spokesperson denies this, saying a drone hit Yanbu pumping station and three cruise missiles targeted Riyadh airport.
notes.key: claim:saudi led coalition and houthi military
notes.claim_by: party:Saudi-led coalition and Houthi military spokesperson

notes.fact: Houthi-run Saba says at least 43 people killed in a Saudi-led strike were buried in Sanaa. The Houthi health ministry claims 359 civilians killed in the latest escalation. CNN could not reach Saudi officials.
notes.key: claim:houthi run saba news agency and houthi health
notes.claim_by: party:Houthi-run Saba news agency and Houthi health ministry

notes.fact: A US-based outlet, citing WHO, says Yemen fighting casualties reached 11,755 by Nov 8, including 2,098 deaths, with over 320,000 displaced since Aug 1. This exceeds the 1,600+ UN count in the hotspot list.

Gaza's civil defence says an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital's surgical wing killed at least six, including a surgeon, and wounded about 20. Israel's military says it targeted a senior Hamas commander.
Israel's military says the second floor was a Hamas headquarters, that Muhammad Abu Ismail was targeted, and that warnings were given. It has not confirmed his death; Hamas denies using the hospital.
Turkish broadcaster TRT says Hamas accuses the Board of Peace of echoing Israel's account. Palestinian authorities cite 1,622 Palestinians killed since the Oct 10, 2025 ceasefire began.
AFP, via Ireland's TheJournal, says Israeli fire killed 11 in Gaza on Thursday and the hospital strike was the deadliest since Israel's election. The army did not confirm the commander's death.
UN special coordinator ad interim Alakbarov said he was deeply alarmed by the strike and warned rising military operations jeopardise the increasingly fragile ceasefire.
AFRICOM says it carried out an airstrike on al-Shabaab on Nov 5 near Jamaame, about 40 km northeast of Kismayo, coordinated with Somalia's government. No casualty details were given.
FDD's Long War Journal says Ugandan troops began leaving Somalia and US troops pulled out of Baledogle airfield, which Turkey may take over. It says this is not a full US withdrawal.
notes.event: Uganda withdrawal and US base exit

notes.fact: New America counts 28 declared AFRICOM strikes on al-Shabaab and none on ISIS-Somalia since May 6. Strikes averaged 5.4 a month June-October, versus 12.6 a month January-May.
Somali outlets say US aircraft struck ISIS positions in Puntland's Qandala district on Nov 9; AFRICOM has not confirmed it. Single-source reporting.
notes.event: Reported US strikes on ISIS in Puntland

notes.fact: Trump posted that Mexico's tariffs will be immediately doubled unless it stops migrant caravans. Sheinbaum said Mexico will use persuasion, not force.
notes.key: claim:us president trump and mexican president sheinbaum
notes.claim_by: party:US President Trump and Mexican President Sheinbaum

notes.fact: The Washington Post says higher prices were a major voter concern and further tariffs would likely push them up. It frames the threat as a return to a familiar Trump theme.

CISA, FBI and three departments warned of malicious activity on industrial refrigeration and cold-chain controllers worldwide. They urged US operators to remove controllers from the internet, change passwords and isolate OT networks. Same equipment is used in the US.

France's blood agency EFS confirmed a refrigeration vendor incident that altered temperature and defrost settings at three blood-storage sites. No attribution given in this report; same controller types exist in US hospitals.
notes.hotspot: cyber: european blood bank cold storage

notes.fact: NPR reports Health-ISAC warned the sector after the French blood bank attack, urging hospitals to separate refrigeration controllers from IT networks and keep manual controls and offline backups.
notes.hotspot: cyber: european blood bank cold storage

notes.fact: FBI says attackers accessed internet-connected PLCs at US water utilities and changed passwords and IP addresses. Reports list at least 12 states; Iran-linked actors are suspected, not formally attributed; no widespread supply interruptions reported.

Al Jazeera says a July attack hit 30+ Minnesota water systems; officials suspected Iran-aligned hackers. A cyberattack attributed to Iran-linked hackers also took a small British power plant offline for four days that month.
notes.event: US water and UK power plant attacks

notes.fact: UK NCSC's annual report counts 80 nationally significant incidents in the year to September 2026 and expects at least one AI-malware attack on critical infrastructure by 2028.
notes.hotspot: cyber: UK NCSC State of the Cyber Nation

notes.fact: CISA added Cisco BroadWorks flaw CVE-2026-20320, used by telecom carriers, to its exploited-vulnerabilities list; federal agencies must patch by Nov 24. Malbear Labs says an autonomous AI agent exploited it.
CISA added four exploited flaws, including an OpenSSH authentication bypass seen in attacks since Nov 6. Actors and scale are unknown; federal patch deadline was Nov 12.
